subject: mathematics
question_text: Let A = {1, 2, 5, 7, 9} and let R be the relation defined on A by x R y if and only if x = y. Find the ordered pairs that belong to R, and find (i) the domain of R and (ii) the range of R.

mark_split.label: List the ordered pairs of R
Write the domain and the range

recall_prompt: Say how you would do this one — say which pairs the condition x = y allows, and where the domain and the range are read from.

page_header: Section A — Very Short Answer Question

steps.label: List the ordered pairs of R
steps.margin_note: First mark. All five pairs must be on the page; one missing pair costs the mark.
lines: A pair belongs to R only when its two members are the same number.
So pair each member of A with itself:

recall.must_convey: That x = y allows only the pairs of a member with itself, giving five pairs.
accept: each member is related only to itself so the pairs are one one two two and so on
x equals y means pair every element with itself
there are five ordered pairs, one for each member of A
prathi element ni daani tho ne jodinchali, five pairs vasthayi
R is the identity relation on A

steps.why: The condition x = y admits only pairs in which a member of A stands with itself, so R has exactly as many pairs as A has members. This relation is called the identity relation on A.
common_mistakes: Listing pairs such as (1, 2) that do not satisfy x = y.
Writing the members 1, 2, 5, 7, 9 instead of the ordered pairs (1, 1), (2, 2) and so on.
Giving all 25 pairs of A × A.
steps.memory_tip: x = y pairs every member with itself and with nothing else, so R has one pair per member of A.

steps.label: Write the domain and the range
steps.margin_note: Second mark. Answer (i) and (ii) separately, even though the two sets turn out to be the same here.
lines: The domain of R is the set of first members of its pairs.
The range of R is the set of second members of its pairs.

lines.text: ∴ (i) domain of R = {1, 2, 5, 7, 9} = A   and   (ii) range of R = {1, 2, 5, 7, 9} = A

recall.must_convey: That both the domain and the range are {1, 2, 5, 7, 9}, that is A itself.
accept: domain is the first coordinates and range is the second coordinates
both come out as the whole set A
domain equals range equals one two five seven nine
domain modati coordinates, range rendava coordinates, rendu A ne
every member of A appears in both, so both are A

steps.why: Every member of A appears as a first coordinate and also as a second coordinate, so the domain and the range are both the whole of A.
common_mistakes: Giving the domain as A × A rather than as a set of numbers.
Leaving a member such as 9 out of one of the two sets.
Writing the range as a single number instead of a set.
steps.memory_tip: Domain is read down the left of the pairs and range down the right — first coordinates, then second coordinates.
